issues.description: Forward-reference string type 'FrameProcessor' on dataclass field has no import and will break runtime introspection
issues.detail: The new `service: "FrameProcessor"` field uses a string annotation but `FrameProcessor` is never imported in frames.py. Anything calling `typing.get_type_hints()` or `dataclasses.fields()` with resolution will blow up. Import it under `TYPE_CHECKING` or use a proper type. Don't ship a type annotation that points at nothing.

issues.description: Putting a live FrameProcessor object inside a Frame is the wrong shape
issues.detail: Frames are data passed through a pipeline. Stuffing a mutable processor reference into one couples the frame's identity to a live object, breaks serialization, complicates logging/replay, and invites cycles. Use a stable identifier (name/id) and resolve it at the switcher. The whole pipeline assumes frames are values; don't smuggle pointers.

issues.description: Identity comparison via `==` on FrameProcessor instead of `is` invites subtle bugs
issues.detail: `if frame.service == self.strategy.active_service` relies on default object equality, which happens to work but is misleading. If anyone ever overrides `__eq__` on a processor subclass, this silently changes behavior. Use `is` — you mean identity, say identity.

issues.description: Renaming a public Frame class with no deprecation alias is a gratuitous break
issues.detail: `RequestMetadataFrame` was exported from `pipecat.frames.frames`. Renaming it without leaving `RequestMetadataFrame = ServiceSwitcherRequestMetadataFrame` as a deprecated alias breaks every downstream import for zero gain. The changelog entry is one line; that's not enough. Either keep an alias for a release or own that this is a breaking change loudly.

issues.description: Comment in push_frame is now subtly wrong about what gets suppressed
issues.detail: The docstring says it suppresses the frame "targeting the active service (since it has already been handled)." Fine. But frames targeting an *inactive* service will now leak out of the switcher untouched — that may be intended (it's the whole point of the rename) but the docstring doesn't say so. State the invariant explicitly so the next maintainer doesn't guess.

issues.description: Duplicated handler logic in STTService and MockMetadataService should be factored
issues.detail: Both `STTService.process_frame` and `MockMetadataService.process_frame` now do the same dance: handle the request, push the metadata, then push the frame onward. If this pattern is the contract for any service receiving the request frame, document it once and provide a base helper. Otherwise every future service author will copy-paste and one will forget the push.

review.summary: The rename is fine; the design is half-baked. Stashing a live `FrameProcessor` reference inside a control frame is the wrong shape — frames should be values, and the unresolved string annotation `"FrameProcessor"` with no import proves the author already sensed the coupling problem. The equality check on processor instances should be `is`, not `==`. Renaming a public frame class with no deprecation alias is a needless break for downstream users. The core idea (target a specific service so the frame can propagate) is right; the implementation needs one more pass.
